text: Mulch and compost are valuable tools for gardeners seeking to enhance soil health. Mulch, made from materials such as wood chips, straw, or plastic, provides a physical barrier that traps soil moisture, suppresses weeds, moderates soil temperature, and adds organic matter. Compost, enriched with organic waste products, enriches the soil with nutrients, improves its structure, and fosters a thriving microbe population that sustains plant health. By regularly applying these natural enrichment methods, gardeners create a fertile environment that supports vigorous, healthy plant growth. Composting specifically can reduce landfill waste and promote circular economy practices, while mulch aids in weed control and water conservation. When gardeners incorporate both mulch and compost into their gardening routine, they build a sustainable soil system that is better equipped to handle various environmental challenges and produce bountiful harvests.
